name: Nucleus-Image
purpose: Text-to-image model testing whether a sparse MoE diffusion transformer reaches leading quality with about 2B active parameters. Released as a base model without post-training.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0; the HF repo has no LICENSE file and the vendor's GitHub repo LICENSE was not reachable (404 on raw), so the text itself was not read.

architecture.kind: sparse MoE diffusion transformer, expert-choice routing
architecture.why_this_design: Expert-choice routing balances experts without auxiliary losses; a decoupled router sees the unmodulated token plus timestep so modulation does not collapse selection; text tokens stay out of the backbone and only contribute KV, enabling text-KV caching across denoising steps; progressive resolution training 256-512-1024. 29 of 32 blocks are MoE (64 routed + 1 shared), first 3 dense. Text encoder Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, Qwen-Image 16-channel VAE.

variants.notes: size incl. 8B text encoder per research/52

pc-16gb.notes: only with quantization and offload; no engine No consumer-GPU speed found.

mac-64gb+.notes: BF16 fits in unified memory; PyTorch only

engine_support.notes: stable-diffusion.cpp PR #2315 and issue #1421 were open on 2026-11-15, not merged.

weaknesses: all 64 experts are touched in every layer at image-token batch sizes, so MoE saves compute, not memory (research/52 estimate)
base model without DPO/RL, 50 steps with CFG

tona_fit.reason: Apache-2.0 by tag, strong GenEval 0.87 / DPG 88.79 (vendor), but a 17B MoE at 51.7 GB BF16 with no engine and no GGUF; revisit when quantized files exist.
